evidence.observation: The ai package's npm scripts define the whole model pipeline. `generate-models` (line 56) runs `node scripts/generate-models.ts --strict`, the network-backed full regeneration that fetches models.dev/OpenRouter/AI-Gateway/Radius and rewrites both the committed TypeScript shards and the ignored JSON data. `hydrate-model-data` (line 57) is the same generator with `--strict --data-only`, which only re-emits the JSON data directory from the already-committed provider list (still network-backed). `generate-model-catalog` (line 58) is `--strict --json-only --json-output ../../.artifacts/model-catalog`, producing the publishable bundle. `check:model-data` (line 59) validates the generated JSON without any fetch, `build` (line 60) chains generate-models then build:offline, and `build:offline` (line 61) is `check:model-data && tsgo -p tsconfig.build.json && cp -r src/providers/data dist/providers/data` — no network call.

The `build` script (line 60) = generate-models + build:offline, i.e. refresh-then-build. `build:offline` (line 61) is the offline-safe path: it only validates the already-present generated data (`check:model-data`), compiles with tsgo, and copies `src/providers/data` into `dist/providers/data`. It performs zero network fetches, so it is safe to run in an air-gapped environment as long as the data directory has been hydrated ahead of time.

validateBundle is the offline gatekeeper for publishing. It reads the generated bundle purely from local files (models.json, models.all.json, providers.json, and the per-provider shards under providers/) and enforces structural invariants: provider index equals the sorted providers of models.all.json (102-105), the required providers anthropic/openai/openrouter are present (109-111), provider shards are byte-equal to models.all.json (120-123), model identity is unique per type (124-138), the legacy models.json is exactly the chat projection of models.all.json (140-147), shard file names match the index (150-154), and at least MINIMUM_MODEL_COUNT=500 chat models exist (155-157). It computes a content-addressed sha256 revision over models.all.json (159-161) so downstream uploads can be skipped when unchanged. No network is used here.

main wires the local-only validation to the optional network publish. It calls validateBundle on the resolved --input directory (line 266) and always writes a local publication.json manifest (line 282). With `--dry-run` it prints the manifest and returns without uploading (285-288), making `npm run check:model-catalog` a fully offline validation of the generated catalog. Only in non-dry-run mode does it touch the network: it shells out to the `aws` CLI via downloadIndex/uploadJson to read the existing index and upload revision objects plus index.json to S3/R2 (290-324). gitSourceCommit (178-182) and the aws helper (184-198) are the only external-process dependencies, and both are bypassed by --dry-run/--source-commit.

buildIndex constructs the ModelCatalogIndex document: it keeps any existing catalog entries whose minimumPiVersion differs, appends the new entry stamped with MINIMUM_PI_VERSION and the freshly computed revision, sorts by semver precedence, and re-validates through parseModelCatalogIndex (the exact parser pi.dev uses). This is local, deterministic bookkeeping that determines which catalog revision a given pi client version receives at runtime; it requires no network beyond the optional index download done earlier in main.

generateModels always awaits the upstream fetches (models.dev chat, models.dev classifier, OpenRouter, Cloudflare AI Gateway, Radius) at 2648-2654, regardless of --data-only. This is why `hydrate:model-data` and `generate:model-catalog` are network-backed: they regenerate content from live catalogs. Only the local `check:model-data` / `build:offline` stage avoids the network, consuming the committed TS shards and the hydrated JSON data directory.

validateGeneratedModelData is the no-network validator behind `check:model-data`. It derives the expected structure from the committed TypeScript provider shards (readModelDataStructure reads src/models.generated.ts imports and the *.models.ts files) and compares it against the on-disk src/providers/data JSON plus .manifest.json hashes. This lets the offline build verify the hydrated data matches the committed catalog without contacting any upstream.

parseModelCatalogIndex is the dependency-free validator pi.dev and pi both use; publish-model-catalog.mjs imports it (along with MODEL_CATALOG_PREFIX, MODEL_CATALOG_SCHEMA_VERSION, getModelCatalogArtifactKey, getModelCatalogProviderKey and compareModelCatalogPiVersions, lines 15-23) to validate and build the index offline. The file header (lines 1-26) documents the storage layout under MODEL_CATALOG_PREFIX and states it is copied verbatim into pi.dev, keeping it free of imports and runtime-specific APIs so it runs unchanged in Node.js and Cloudflare Workers — which is what lets the local validation and the hosted serving logic agree without network access.

The Development section documents the intended split: `npm run build` refreshes model data then builds, while `npm run build:offline` rebuilds using existing model data without network access. This is the user-facing statement of the offline contract implemented by packages/ai.

The release source-archive script hard-requires generated model data to already exist: it checks for packages/ai/src/providers/data/.manifest.json (82-84) and for the provider JSON files (85-92), erroring with "Run npm run hydrate:model-data first" otherwise. This confirms the JSON data directory is a hydrated (not committed) build input that must be produced before offline/packaged builds.

CI hydrates network-fetched model data once (`npm run hydrate:model-data`) before creating the release source archive, so that downstream standalone-binary builds can use `--offline-model-data` and the committed/archived data instead of contacting upstream catalogs.

The catalog workflow runs `npm run generate:model-catalog` (network) to build .artifacts/model-catalog, then `npm run check:model-catalog` (offline dry-run of publish-model-catalog.mjs) to validate it, and uploads the artifact; a separate publish job (using the aws CLI against Cloudflare R2) performs the only network upload. So generation is network-bound, validation is offline, and publication is a guarded, separately-gated step.

claims.claim: packages/ai/package.json defines three distinct model inputs with different network requirements: `generate-models` and `hydrate-model-data` are network-backed generators of the ignored JSON data, `generate-model-catalog` is a network-backed generator of the publishable bundle under .artifacts/, and `check:model-data` is a no-network validator.

The offline-safe build path is `build:offline`, which validates the already-hydrated data with `check:model-data`, compiles with tsgo, and copies src/providers/data into dist — it performs no fetch, so `npm run build:offline` succeeds without network once the data directory exists.

The generated TypeScript provider shards (src/providers/*.models.ts, src/models.generated.ts) are committed to the repository, but the JSON data directory packages/ai/src/providers/data/ is gitignored and therefore must be hydrated before offline or release builds.

scripts/publish-model-catalog.mjs separates offline validation from network publication: validateBundle and buildIndex operate purely on local generated files, main always writes publication.json, and `--dry-run` (used by `npm run check:model-catalog`) returns before any S3/R2 upload.

validateBundle enforces the publishable-bundle contract entirely offline: required providers, per-provider shard equality, chat-projection equality of models.json, unique typed identities, and the MINIMUM_MODEL_COUNT=500 floor, then derives a content-addressed sha256 revision over models.all.json so unchanged catalogs are not re-uploaded.

Only the publish/upload step and the upstream-catalog fetches require network; the deterministic revision and index selection logic lives in scripts/model-catalog-protocol.ts, which is dependency-free and shared with pi.dev so it runs identically in Node and Cloudflare Workers.

conclusion: The pi model pipeline splits into three tiers. (1) Generated: `npm run generate-models` (packages/ai/package.json:56) is the full, network-backed regeneration of the committed TypeScript shards (src/providers/*.models.ts, src/models.generated.ts) plus the ignored JSON data under src/providers/data/. (2) Hydrated: `npm run hydrate:model-data` (line 57) re-emits only that JSON data directory (--data-only) using the existing provider list; it is still network-backed, and because the data dir is gitignored (verified: absent in this checkout and untracked) it must be run before any offline-packed build — the release source-archive script and build-binaries workflow both gate on it. (3) Offline-safe: `npm run build:offline` (line 61) only validates the hydrated data against the committed TS catalog via `check:model-data`, compiles, and copies the data into dist, with no fetch — matching README's "without network access". The publishable catalog bundle is generated network-side by `generate:model-catalog` into .artifacts/model-catalog, then validated fully offline by scripts/publish-model-catalog.mjs in --dry-run (validateBundle enforces structural invariants and computes a sha256 revision from local bytes). Network is touched only by the four upstream fetches in generate-models.ts:2648-2654 and by the aws-CLI uploads inside main() (lines 290-324), which --dry-run skips. Therefore inputs safe to use offline are: the committed TypeScript model shards, the hydrated src/providers/data JSON + .manifest.json, and the generated .artifacts/model-catalog bundle; the only non-offline inputs are the live models.dev/OpenRouter/AI-Gateway/Radius catalog fetches and the S3/R2 upload path.
